text: This man's elevator cable just snapped, and he's dropping down the shaft.
He floats, because he's falling as fast as the car.
Movies say: jump right before it hits.
Bad news: from ten floors, he'd hit at over fifty miles an hour.
His best jump takes off about seven. And he can't see the bottom coming.
Good news: real elevators hang on four to eight steel cables, and just one can hold the car.
Too fast? Brakes clamp the rails and stop him.
In nineteen forty-five, a woman fell seventy-five floors in the Empire State Building, and lived.
Squeezed air and coiled cable slowed her down.
And that's what really happens when an elevator cable snaps.
